question: Can a Customer Have Multiple WooCommerce Subscriptions at Once?
metaDescription: Yes, by default — each product purchase creates its own independent subscription. Here's how that works and where it commonly trips up store owners.
shortAnswer: Yes. WooCommerce Subscriptions doesn't limit customers to one active subscription — each subscription product purchased creates its own independent subscription record, with its own billing schedule, status, and payment method. A customer can have several running at once, whether that's several different products or multiple purchases of the same one.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

Every time a subscription product is purchased, a new subscription entity is created and linked to that customer, entirely independent of any subscriptions they already hold. My Account → Subscriptions lists all of them together, but each one manages its own status, next payment date, and payment method separately — cancelling one has no effect on the others.

Where This Trips Up Store Owners

  • Assuming one payment-method update applies everywhere. Updating the card on one subscription doesn't update it on the customer's other subscriptions — each one stores its own payment token independently.
  • Wanting to limit a customer to a single active plan (common for tiered membership models, where a second purchase should replace rather than add to the first). That restriction isn't built in and needs custom logic to enforce at checkout.
  • Confusing multiple subscriptions with multiple items on one subscription. A single subscription with several products isn't the same as several separate subscriptions — the built-in support for grouping multiple products under one recurring order depends on how the cart was structured at checkout.
  • Reporting or renewal reminders that don't account for a customer having several subscriptions, potentially causing confusing overlapping notifications if not accounted for in email templates or third-party integrations.

What to Check

  1. For a customer confused about which subscription a charge belongs to, each subscription's own order history and ID make it possible to trace a specific charge back to its source — useful when handling a support enquiry.
  2. To enforce a single-active-subscription-per-customer rule, that requires custom checkout validation checking for existing active subscriptions before allowing a new purchase.
  3. For bundling multiple products under one recurring bill rather than separate subscriptions, the cart needs to combine subscription products in a way WooCommerce Subscriptions treats as a single multi-item subscription — worth testing carefully, since it depends on matching billing schedules across the products involved.

See custom WooCommerce development for subscription-limit rules or bundled-billing setups the built-in plugin doesn't handle out of the box.
